title: Make it easier to use `ir` with `Rapp`
description:
There should be a simple cli entry point for usage in shebangs. Currently there are two ways that work, but one requires all dependencies to be declared in the opening shebang, and the other requires some unsightly boilerplate. 

```r
#!/usr/bin/env -S rx --from github::r-lib/Rapp --with glue Rapp
#| name: greet
#| description: Print a greeting.

#| description: Person to greet.
name <- "world"

#| description: Number of greetings.
n <- 1L

cat(rep(glue::glue("Hello, {name}!"), n), sep = "\n")[5:01 PM]You can set the shebang to rx Rapp
```

The other way around, you can use `ir` as the entry point, and then invoke `Rapp` manually

```r
#!/usr/bin/env -S ir run
#| packages:
#|   - github::r-lib/Rapp
#|   - glue
#| isolated: true
#| name: greet
#| description: Print a greeting.

# On the initial Rscript invocation, hand this file to Rapp.
if (!interactive() && sys.nframe() == 0L) {
  script <- sub(
    "^--file=", "",
    grep("^--file=", commandArgs(), value = TRUE)[1L]
  )
  Rapp::run(script, args = commandArgs(TRUE))
  quit(save = "no", status = 0L)
}

#| description: Person to greet.
name <- "world"

#| description: Number of greetings.
n <- 1L

cat(rep(glue::glue("Hello, {name}!"), n), sep = "\n")
```



Neither of these is great. Ideally we could have a normal yaml frontmatter, with a simple shebang invocation. Maybe something like:

```r
#!/usr/bin/env -S rx Rapp
#| packages:
#|   - glue
#| isolated: true
#| name: greet
#| description: Print a greeting.

#| description: Person to greet.
name <- "world"

#| description: Number of greetings.
n <- 1L

cat(rep(glue::glue("Hello, {name}!"), n), sep = "\n")
```

title: Command to generate the frontmatter?
description:
I might be missing something about the usual workflow when using `ir` (tbh, I have just quickly tried it), but shouldn't there be a command to automatically generate the frontmatter? I don't think `uv` has this but they have [some kind of automation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/scripts/#declaring-script-dependencies) with `uv add --script example.py 'requests<3' 'rich'`.

I don't want to type the entire frontmatter or to copy it from the docs every time. It would be nice to have `ir add-template script.R` (probably with a better command name) that would automatically add this:

```
#!/usr/bin/env -S ir run
#| packages:
#|   - <to fill with packages loaded in the script and their used versions>
#| r-version: ">= <my current R version>"
#| isolated: true
```

I can then choose to tweak this frontmatter or not. That way, I can take any existing standalone script and instantly add the info used by `ir`.

I can also imagine `ir run` giving a message `No frontmatter found in <script.R>. Use ir add-template to add one`.

title: Feature request: allow users to specify a setup shell script/batch file to install additional kernels and engines
description:
Most alternative jupyter kernels/Quarto engines only usually only require running a few lines of setup code.

Could you allow users to specify such code in say an `ir-setup.sh`/`ir-setup.bat` file (or whatever name you prefer) - you could then run that file before the `quarto render`/`quarto preview` call.

For example,

* With ark, you need to download then run the install command
  ```sh
  # Download a release from https://github.com/posit-dev/ark/releases
  ark --install
  ```
* For the IRkernel you'd need the IRkernel R package and its setup line
  ```sh
  R -e "install.packages('IRkernel'); IRkernel::installspec()"
  ```
* With the nbstata Stata kernel, you need the nbstata Python package and then a Python command run within that environment
  ```sh
  # activate venv
  uv pip install nbstata
  python3 -m nbstata.install # --sys-prefix
  ```
* For the julia jupyter kernel install Julia with say [`juliaup`](https://github.com/JuliaLang/juliaup) then install the IJulia package within Julia
  ```sh
  juliaup self update
  juliaup default release
  julia -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.add("IJulia")'
  ```
* I guess for Quarto docs with `engine: julia` you just need to make sure Julia is installed with `juliaup` and then I think Quarto auto installs the engine if it's not there
  ```sh
  juliaup self update
  juliaup default release
  ```

(etc., you get the idea)

title: Package install messages go to stdout instead of stderr
description:
## Summary

`ir` writes package resolution and installation progress to stdout rather than stderr. This makes it impossible to cleanly capture or pipe script output when packages need to be installed on first run.

## Minimal example

```sh
# Use a fresh cache to force package resolution
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
IR_CACHE_DIR="$tmp" ir run --with glue -e 'cat("hello\n")' > out.txt 2>/dev/null
cat out.txt
```

**Expected** (`out.txt`):
```
hello
```

**Actual** (`out.txt`):
```
The following package(s) will be installed:
- glue [1.8.1]
These packages will be installed into "/tmp/tmp.abc123/libraries/...".

# Installing packages --------------------------------------------------------
✔ glue 1.8.1                              [linked from cache]
Successfully installed 1 package in 5 milliseconds.
hello
```

## Why this matters

- Piping `ir run script.R | next_command` sends package install messages into the downstream command's input
- Redirecting stderr with `2>/dev/null` does not suppress the noise since it's on stdout
- Tools that invoke `ir` as a subprocess (e.g., using processx with `stderr = NULL`) cannot filter the output without also capturing and parsing the script's actual output

## Expected behavior

Package resolution and installation progress should go to stderr, matching the Unix convention that stdout is for program output (data) and stderr is for diagnostics/progress.

## Version

```
$ ir --version
ir 0.1.0
```

title: minimize pak calls
Remove rscript from frontmatter metadata
description:
## Context

In https://github.com/t-kalinowski/ir/pull/90#discussion_r3467210162, Christophe pointed out that frontmatter `rscript:` makes self-describing files less reproducible because it can encode a machine-specific executable path or command.

`r-version` is a better fit for source metadata because it describes the required R version and lets `rig` resolve the local executable. `rscript` is still useful as an operator override when someone wants to run or resolve with a specific local Rscript without editing the file.

## Proposed change

Remove support for `rscript` from script and Quarto frontmatter metadata.

Keep these supported:

- `--rscript <path-or-command>`
- `IR_RSCRIPT=<path-or-command>`

These should continue to act as overrides over frontmatter, including frontmatter `r-version`.

## Expected behavior

- Frontmatter should no longer select R via `rscript:`.
- Prefer failing fast with a clear error if frontmatter contains `rscript:`, since this key used to be meaningful and silently ignoring it would be surprising.
- `--rscript` should still override `IR_R_VERSION` and frontmatter `r-version`.
- `IR_RSCRIPT` should still override frontmatter `r-version`.
- Existing CLI and environment conflict behavior should remain unchanged:
  - `--r-version` with `--rscript` errors.
  - `IR_R_VERSION` with `IR_RSCRIPT` errors.

## Docs to update

- README reproducibility/requirements language
- `docs/run.qmd` frontmatter metadata section
- `docs/config.qmd` R selection precedence/configuration language
- Any help snapshots only if CLI text changes, but the CLI flags should stay.

## Tests

Add or update public CLI tests covering:

- frontmatter `rscript:` is rejected with the new message
- `IR_RSCRIPT` still overrides frontmatter `r-version`
- `--rscript` still overrides frontmatter `r-version`

description:
It may not end up a public API but if we do this tools like quarto could use 'ir' for R and python to boostrap an environment based on config.

This would be required for using 'quarto render' directly instead of `ir run <.qmd>`. 

It is just an idea to have all related code logic in the same place. But we could also decide to scope ir to R only.

title: Support R package `bin/` executables in `ir tool install` and `rx`
description:
`ir tool install` and `rx` currently support tools installed from package `exec/`, but not package `bin/`. R packages can install executable binaries under `bin` or `bin/<arch>` via `src/install.libs.R`, so `ir` should support both locations.

## Requested behavior

- Tool discovery should include:
  - installed package `exec/`
  - installed package `bin/`
  - installed package architecture-specific `bin/<arch>`
- Installed tools should be symlinked from the configured user-facing bin directory, e.g. `~/.local/bin`, to the installed package executable.
- `rx` should be able to resolve and run tools from both `exec/` and `bin/`.

https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Package-subdirectories-1

title: Design non-R CLI tool installs for `ir tool`
description:
Longer term, `ir tool install` should work well for CLI tools that are not R packages.

Example target:

```sh
ir tool install yamark
```

for `~/github/t-kalinowski/yamark`.

That repo should be installable without requiring an R package at the repository root.

## Open design

Possible designs:

- Search common package locations, e.g. `r/DESCRIPTION`, `r-pkg/DESCRIPTION`, or the first `DESCRIPTION`.
- Support explicit project metadata such as `ir.toml` or `project.toml`.
- Recognize common build/install ecosystems such as Cargo projects.
- Prefer downloading prebuilt GitHub release binaries for Cargo projects, rather than building from source on user machines.

This needs design before implementation.

title: Add GitHub shorthand for R packages in `ir tool install` and `ir tool run`
description:
`ir tool` currently resolves package names, but it should also support GitHub shorthand for R packages.

## Requested behavior

Add resolver behavior:

- `ir tool install foo` -> CRAN package `foo`
- `ir tool install foo/bar` -> GitHub repo `foo/bar`
- `ir tool run foo` -> CRAN package `foo`
- `ir tool run foo/bar` -> GitHub repo `foo/bar`

For GitHub repos, `ir` should find and install an R package from the repository. A first version can require a root `DESCRIPTION`; later versions can support common subdirectory layouts.

## Scope

This issue is only about GitHub shorthand for R packages.

Non-R CLI tools should be handled separately.

title: Windows CI: #39 e2e fixture tests fail on the GitHub runner
description:
Since #39 added the real-toolchain fixture tests, the `test (windows-latest)` CI job fails several of them. They don't reproduce on a single-drive local Windows box — the root causes are specific to the GitHub Actions runner environment.

## Status

- [x] `os error 123` — quarto `--output-dir` cross-drive join (#52)
  - [x] `run_quarto_fixture_renders_html_with_resolved_packages`
- [x] Availability probe co-loaded all 16 packages and crashed (#56)
  - [x] `ci_dependencies_are_available` — reframed to `find.package`, no co-load
- [ ] `0xC0000005` — native crash when multiple packages co-load in one R session
  - [ ] `run_inline_expression_resolves_with_dependencies`
  - [ ] `run_script_fixture_resolves_packages_and_isolates_user_library`
  - [ ] `tool_install_installs_real_package_entrypoint`
- [ ] reticulate cannot find the runner Python
  - [ ] `run_reticulate_fixture_imports_python_module`

The four open tests are skipped on Windows via `#[cfg_attr(windows, ignore)]` in #56 so the job is not permanently red while these are investigated. They still run on Linux and macOS.

## `0xC0000005` — native co-load crash

- `run_inline_expression_resolves_with_dependencies`
- `run_script_fixture_resolves_packages_and_isolates_user_library`
- `tool_install_installs_real_package_entrypoint` (depends on the same resolution path)

Diagnosis on the debug branch established: every fixture package loads cleanly in its own `Rscript` process, but loading them together in one session faults with `0xC0000005`. It is a native DLL interaction between two co-loaded packages, not an ABI mismatch (`secretbase` loads fine alone) and not sessioninfo (dev `sessioninfo 1.2.3.9000` was installed and the crash persisted; these tests never call `platform_info()`). The crash discards all in-process output — stdout, stderr, and even per-line file flushes — so pinning the exact conflicting pair needs cross-process bisection on a runner-like Windows environment. `ci_dependencies_are_available` was a self-inflicted instance of this (16-way co-load) and is fixed in #56 by not loading the namespaces at all; the `ir`-path tests reach the crash through real resolution and still need root-causing.

## reticulate cannot find the runner Python

- `run_reticulate_fixture_imports_python_module`

The test installs reticulate and friends, then exits 1 — reticulate does not discover the runner's Python (`Installation of Python not found, Python bindings not loaded`). #48 removed the reticulate cache overrides but the Windows discovery failure remains. Likely needs the concrete interpreter path (e.g. `sys.executable` / `RETICULATE_PYTHON`) on the runner.

## Resolved

- Cross-drive `--output-dir` join (#52): render a copy of each fixture in its own temp dir and drop `--output-dir`, so quarto writes beside the input and the path stays single-drive.
- Availability probe (#56): `find.package` instead of co-loading all namespaces.
- Dev sessioninfo (#54, closed): ruled out — does not fix the crash.

title: Resolver trusts an inherited `R_LIBS_USER` from a different R, breaking `--r-version`
description:
When `ir run --r-version <v>` selects an R that differs from the one on `PATH`, the resolver still inherits the caller's `R_LIBS_USER`. If that library was built for the default R, the selected R loads ABI-incompatible compiled packages from it — `secretbase` in particular, which `ir_input_key()` reaches first.

The resolver session is spawned with the ambient environment intact (`resolve_library_inner` in `src/main.rs` sets no `R_LIBS_USER`).

#45's tooling bootstrap keys its own library by R version and platform, but decides what to install with `requireNamespace()` over the full `.libPaths()`, which still includes the inherited `R_LIBS_USER`:

```r
ir_missing_tooling <- function(packages = ir_tooling_packages())
  Filter(function(p) !requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE), packages)
```

So when the inherited library already holds `secretbase` (built for a different R), the probe either reuses the mismatched build or crashes in the `requireNamespace()` load itself before any tooling is installed.

Reproducible in CI: `r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies` exports `R_LIBS_USER` at the default R's cache; selecting a rig-managed 4.4.3 then fails two ways:

- Linux: `secretbase.so: undefined symbol: ANY_ATTRIB` at load (a 4.5-built `.so` under 4.4.3)
- macOS: segfault in `secretbase::sha256` (lazy-bound, so the fault surfaces at the call)

```
*** caught segfault ***
address 0x180, cause 'invalid permissions'
Traceback:
 1: secretbase::sha256(...)
 2: ir_input_key(deps, exclude_newer = exclude_newer)
```

We could drop `R_LIBS_USER` for the resolver when the selected R differs from the default (or always, now that #45 bootstraps its own tooling), so the requested R only sees its version-keyed libraries. A real `--r-version` user usually has no `R_LIBS_USER` exported, which is why this only bites environments that set it (CI, some configured setups).

PR #38's end-to-end `--r-version` tests work around this by dropping `R_LIBS_USER` before invoking `ir`; this issue tracks handling it in `ir` itself.

Refs #45, #27.

title: Trim serde footprint: parse rig JSON via serde_json::Value instead of derive
description:
### Summary

Trim the serde footprint added in #18 by parsing the two `rig … --json` shapes with `serde_json::Value` instead of `#[derive(Deserialize)]`, dropping the direct `serde` dependency (and the `derive` feature).

### Why Cargo.toml flags alone don't help

- The code uses `#[derive(Deserialize)]`, so `serde_derive` is mandatory while it stays.
- `default-features = false` on `serde` would break the build — the `String`/`PathBuf`/`Vec` fields rely on serde's `std` impls.
- The heavy crate, `syn`, is **already** pulled in by `thiserror` (via `saphyr`/`saphyr-parser`), so serde never introduced it. `cargo tree -i syn` confirms both `serde_derive` and `thiserror-impl` depend on it.

So the only effective lever is to stop deriving and read the fields off `serde_json::Value`.

### Measured effect

| | serde-stack crates |
|---|---|
| Before | `serde`, `serde_core`, `serde_derive`, `serde_json`, `itoa`, `memchr`, `zmij` (7) |
| After | `serde_core`, `serde_json`, `itoa`, `memchr`, `zmij` (5) |

Removes `serde` + `serde_derive` (the only serde proc-macro codegen step). `syn` stays regardless, so binary size is essentially unchanged — the win is a leaner build graph, not a smaller binary.

**Bonus:** a null/missing `binary` field now yields a clear `` `rig list --json` entry is missing string `binary` `` error instead of an opaque serde failure.

### Honest scope

Modest: one build-time proc-macro crate plus the thin `serde` wrapper, no change to `syn` or binary size, traded for ~30 lines of manual mapping. The error-message/robustness improvement is arguably the better motivation than the crate count.

### Verified

Prototyped on the PR head (`bda1e64`): `cargo build` clean, `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean, all 17 `tests/cli.rs` tests pass.
